description: Rückbeil, Fiona Elena and colleagues publish this resource through Zenodo. The implemented Python tool predicts exhaustion and breakthrough in granular-activated-carbon and ion-exchange treatment. It extends the US EPA pore-surface diffusion formulation with a tracer model for dissolved-organic-matter competition. Inputs include isotherms, internal and external mass transfer and background-organic-matter adsorption. A user interface is supplied, with laboratory testing and pilot-plant validation described by the source. The native archive has MIT terms. Its GitHub pointer identifies an author account, not a verified specific repository, so an exact code-repository identity is not invented. Predictions depend on the supplied substance and treatment parameters. Coverage is limited to the stated models, observations and application settings. Native metadata gives open access and the licence label mit-license. These terms describe the deposit; software and companion-data terms are distinguished where separately established. Only descriptive metadata and file descriptors were inspected; linked data, code and document bodies were not opened.
